QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_9

question.text: A close-ended mutual fund scheme has a fixed maturity period. Under SEBI rules, every close-ended scheme other than an ELSS shall be listed on:

answer.text: A recognized stock exchange to provide liquidity to investors
The AMC's website for direct redemption by investors
Both stock exchange and AMC platform simultaneously
The RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent) platform

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that every close-ended scheme other than an ELSS shall be listed on a recognised stock exchange. Because close-ended funds do not offer continuous repurchase with the AMC, the exchange listing is the principal mechanism through which investors can exit before maturity by selling to another buyer. The Trap: Close-ended funds do not allow redemption through the AMC before maturity, so Options B and C are wrong. The RTA platform in Option D handles servicing rather than acting as the listing venue. Interval funds use periodic transactions with the AMC and are a separate structure. Note: Source pages 45 and 46 support the stock exchange listing requirement for close-ended schemes subject to the ELSS exception.
